text:
Maria G.: Quick brain-dump — proposing a lightweight probe strategy to bring up hetero-quant variants (FP8/AWQ/INT8) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Goal: surface quality deltas early and have automatic, predictable fallback paths. Thoughts?

Ajay Patel: +1 on early probes. We should keep probe traffic tiny but representative. Suggest 1k golden queries + 500 adversarial per probe, rolled hourly for first 24h.

Sophia L.: Agree. Golden set must include our regression-sensitive prompts (billing, instructions, code). Also add synthetic long-context tests. We caught edge-case drift last time with only short prompts.

Kevin H.: Heads-up — private customers often show different latency distribution and token mix. Probes should tag env and model fingerprint so we can compare appless vs customer workloads.

Lucas M.: Draft of a simple routing/fallback snippet for the control plane. Keep it conservative for private:

```
probe_config:
  sample_sets: [golden, adversarial, long_context]
  traffic_rules:
    hosted: {base: 0.95, variant: 0.05}
    dedicated: {base: 0.98, variant: 0.02}
    private: {base: 0.995, variant: 0.005}
  safety_gates:
    quality_delta_auc: 0.015   # fail if delta > 0.015
    latency_p99_pct_increase: 15
  fallback_policy: "route-to-base-if-gate-fires,sticky-rollback:5m"
```

Ajay Patel: I like the thresholds but maybe relax quality gate to 0.02 for FP8 on smaller models where noise is higher. Keep stricter for LLM family >7B.

Maria G.: Good call. We'll parameterize by model class. Proposed rule: use model-size buckets {<=7B, 7B-13B, >13B} with increasing strictness.

Sophia L.: Also: add a golden-set alert that triggers an immediate canary pause + sample-dump for offline eval. Manual intervention for private customers unless they opt into auto-rollback.

Kevin H.: For private, default to manual rollback. Enterprise customers may want auto if they accept risk. Make the opt-in explicit.

Lucas M.: Operational note: include a per-variant holding buffer for KV cache warming. We saw an artificial spike when cold-starting variants last run. Add a warmup window of 30s where traffic goes to variant but is excluded from SLO calculations.

Deploy Bot: canary_run_summary: variant=awq-8bit, model=stella-13b, env=hosted, samples=1500, quality_delta=0.012, latency_p99_increase=8%, status=pass

Maria G.: Nice. That pass would hit a soft-ok for 13B class. Next steps: 1) finalize sample sets (Sophia), 2) tune thresholds by model bucket (Ajay), 3) implement routing snippet with warmup exclusion (Lucas), 4) add opt-in UI flag for private auto-rollback (Kevin). I'll open a RFC with configs and a short eval harness for local dry-run.

Sophia L.: I'll push the golden+adversarial lists to the repo and add long-context generator script.

Ajay Patel: I'll run a small sensitivity sweep tonight across 3 models and post metrics (delta-AUC, top-1 label shifts, BLEU-like code regressions).

Kevin H.: I'll draft the customer-facing opt-in copy + default privacy-safe settings.

Lucas M.: I'll wire the warmup exclusion into the routing service and add observability tags (variant_warmup=true).

Maria G.: Thanks all. If anyone sees a big red flag in the sweeps, ping #eng-oncall and tag me. Otherwise aim to ship the probe RFC by EOD Friday. :rocket:
